The settings of a table style

Source: R/tables.R
jstyle_settings.Rd

Every setting a jstats table style holds: the general settings, which set the look of every table, then one section per table type, which set that table's columns, labels and notes. A style file (see jstyle) sets any of them; a setting it leaves out comes from the style its based.on line names, and in the end from the built-in apa style, whose value each entry gives – with the built-in report style's where it differs. A table type's setting can also be given in a jtable call, for that table only.

This page is made from the list jstats checks every style against, so it names exactly what jstats accepts. A Greek letter in a label is written in a style file as the letter itself; this page names it.

See also

jstyle to list, print and copy styles; jtable for the tables.

In a style file

A setting is its name, an equals sign and a value; a list of values is separated by commas; a # starts a note. The general settings come first, then each table type's under its heading:


based.on = apa
font     = Arial

[regression]
fit.rows = r2, n

To give one table type its own value of a general setting, copy the setting's line under that type's heading and change the value there: it then holds for that table type only. Two exceptions: paper, the page of the whole Word file, is set only at the top, and [plot] takes only a chart's own settings. In a title, a single column's head (such as stub.label or b.label), note.label or source.label, *word* sets a word in italics and ^mark^ a superscript; any other label prints the marks as typed.

General settings

font

the typeface of every cell, caption and note. Takes any text. In apa: Times New Roman; in report: Arial.

size

the text size, in points. Takes a number from 6 to 72. In apa: 12; in report: 10.

paper

the page the file opens on: a4 | letter. Takes one of a4 | letter. In apa: a4.

caption.form

apa: "Table 1" in bold, the title in italics on the next line | journal: "Table 1." in bold, the title after it on the same line, not bold | report: "Table 1:" and the title on one line, both in bold. Takes one of apa | journal | report. In apa: apa; in report: report.

caption.position

row: the table's first row, repeated with the header on a new page | paragraph: above the table. Takes one of row | paragraph. In apa: row.

caption.size

the caption's text size, in points, or size for the text size (size - 1 a point smaller), so it moves when size does. Takes a number from 6 to 72, or size, or size and a number such as size - 1. In apa: size.

caption.fill

a color filling the caption row (caption.position = row), header for the header's fill and text color, or none. Takes a color name such as lightblue, or six hex digits such as ADD8E6; or header, or none. In apa: none.

caption.text

the color of the caption's text (under caption.fill = header, the header's text color). Takes a color name such as lightblue, or six hex digits such as ADD8E6. In apa: 000000.

header.fill

a color filling the header cells, or none. Takes a color name such as lightblue, or six hex digits such as ADD8E6; or none. In apa: none; in report: D9D9D9.

header.text

the color of the header's text. Takes a color name such as lightblue, or six hex digits such as ADD8E6. In apa: 000000.

header.bold

bold header text: yes | no. Takes one of yes | no. In apa: no; in report: yes.

band.fill

a color filling every other data row, or none. Takes a color name such as lightblue, or six hex digits such as ADD8E6; or none. In apa: none.

heading.fill

a color filling each variable's label row (the rows variable.headings sets), or none. Takes a color name such as lightblue, or six hex digits such as ADD8E6; or none. In apa: none.

rules

apa: rules above and below the header and under the table | grid: every cell | outer: a box | none. Takes one of apa | grid | outer | none. In apa: apa.

rule.color

the color of the rules. Takes a color name such as lightblue, or six hex digits such as ADD8E6. In apa: 000000.

note.label

the word the general note opens on: Note. | Notes: | Source:. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: Note.; in report: Note:.

note.label.italic

the note's label in italics, as APA sets it: yes | no. Takes one of yes | no. In apa: yes; in report: no.

note.position

row: the table's last row | paragraph: under the table. Takes one of row | paragraph. In apa: row.

note.size

the notes' text size, in points, or size for the text size (size - 1 a point smaller), so it moves when size does. Takes a number from 6 to 72, or size, or size and a number such as size - 1. In apa: size; in report: size - 1.

note.sentences

paragraph: the general note in one paragraph, as APA sets it | lines: each of its sentences, and each specific note, on a line of its own. Takes one of paragraph | lines. In apa: paragraph; in report: lines.

note.order

apa: the general note, then the specific notes, then the probability note | report: the probability note, the specific notes, then the general note. Takes one of apa | report. In apa: apa; in report: report.

source.position

where a call's source = goes: note (the general note's last sentence) | line (a line of its own, last, after source.label). Takes one of note | line. In apa: note; in report: line.

source.label

the word the source line opens on, upright: Source: | Sources:. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: Source:.

n.position

where N, the number of cases, goes: note (the general note opens on it) | title ("(N = 103)" after the title; a table with several ns, such as Ns that differ or a t test's groups, gives them in the note) | none (no N; a table of models whose Ns differ still says so in its note). Takes one of note | title | none. In apa: title.

decimals

the decimal places of a statistic, such as a mean. Takes a whole number from 0 to 6. In apa: 2.

leading.zero

yes: a zero before the point of every number below 1 (0.23) | no: no zero on a statistic that cannot exceed 1, such as p (.23), and a zero on any other number below 1, such as an SE (0.197); APA's rule | never: no zero before the point of any number (.23 for p, .197 for an SE). Takes one of yes | no | never. In apa: no; in report: yes.

p.format

exact: the p-value in the p column, with no asterisks | stars: asterisks on the statistic (b, t, F or chi-square) and no p column; a table without that statistic keeps a p column of asterisks | both: the p-value and its asterisks in the p column. Takes one of exact | stars | both. In apa: exact.

p.decimals

the decimal places of a p-value. Takes a whole number from 1 to 6. In apa: 3.

stars

the p-values the asterisks mark, largest first. Takes one to three p-values between 0 and 1, largest first. In apa: .05, .01, .001.

marks

the marks of the notes on rows: letters (a, b, c) | symbols (daggers). Takes one of letters | symbols. In apa: letters.

minus

true: a true minus sign | hyphen: the keyboard's hyphen. Takes one of true | hyphen. In apa: true.

thousands

comma: 1,037 | none: 1037. Takes one of comma | none. In apa: comma.

landscape

auto: a landscape page when the table is wider than a portrait one | yes | no. Takes one of auto | yes | no. In apa: auto.

line.spacing

single | double. Takes one of single | double. In apa: single.

percent.decimals

the decimal places of a percentage. Takes a whole number from 0 to 4. In apa: 1.

filter.note

yes: the general note says which cases a filter kept (jsubset(), subset =) | no. Takes one of yes | no. In apa: yes.

[descriptives]: a descriptives table

title

the title when the call gives none. Takes any text. In apa: Descriptive Statistics.

columns

the columns, in order: n, mean, sd, min, max. Takes one or more of n, mean, sd, min, max, in order, separated by commas. In apa: n, mean, sd, min, max.

stub.label

the first column's head. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: Variable.

n.label

the head of the n column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: n.

mean.label

the head of the mean column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: M.

sd.label

the head of the sd column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: SD.

min.label

the head of the min column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: Min.

max.label

the head of the max column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: Max.

group.headings

how a heading from headings = is set: italic | bold | plain. Takes one of italic | bold | plain. In apa: italic.

[frequencies]: a frequency table

title

the title when the call gives none. Takes any text. In apa: Frequency Distributions.

columns

the columns, in order: n, percent (of all cases), valid.percent, cumulative. Takes one or more of n, percent, valid.percent, cumulative, in order, separated by commas. In apa: n, percent.

stub.label

the first column's head. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: Variable.

n.label

the head of the n column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: n.

percent.label

the head of the percent column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: %.

valid.percent.label

the head of the valid.percent column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: Valid %.

cumulative.label

the head of the cumulative column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: Cumulative %.

missing.rows

a variable's missing cases: combined (one row) | each (a row per missing value) | none. Takes one of combined | each | none. In apa: combined.

missing.label

the label of the combined missing row. Takes any text. In apa: Missing.

variable.headings

how each variable's label row is set: plain | italic | bold. Takes one of plain | italic | bold. In apa: plain; in report: bold.

group.headings

how a heading from headings = is set: italic | bold | plain. Takes one of italic | bold | plain. In apa: italic.

[regression]: a regression table

title

the title when the call gives none; {outcome} is the outcome's label. Takes any text. In apa: Regression Coefficients Predicting {outcome}.

columns

the columns of each model, in order: b, se, beta, p, t, ci, beta.gelman (Gelman's standardized coefficient). Takes one or more of b, se, beta, p, t, ci, beta.gelman, in order, separated by commas. In apa: b, se, beta, p.

columns.last

columns added to the last model only, or none. Takes one or more of b, se, beta, p, t, ci, beta.gelman, in order, separated by commas; or none. In apa: none.

stub.label

the first column's head. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: Predictor.

b.label

the head of the b column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: b.

se.label

the head of the se column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: SE.

beta.label

the head of the beta column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: \(\beta\).

p.label

the head of the p column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: p.

t.label

the head of the t column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: t.

ci.label

the head of the ci column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: 95% CI.

beta.gelman.label

the head of the beta.gelman column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: \(\beta\)*.

ci.style

one: the interval in one column, [LL, UL] | two: LL and UL. Takes one of one | two. In apa: one.

intercept

the constant's row, first in the table: yes | no. Takes one of yes | no. In apa: yes.

intercept.label

the constant's row label. Takes any text. In apa: Constant.

fit.rows

the fit rows under the predictors, in order: r2, adj.r2, f, delta.r2 (nested models), f.change (its F test), n, or none. Takes one or more of r2, adj.r2, f, delta.r2, f.change, n, in order, separated by commas; or none. In apa: r2.

reference

where a dummy-coded variable's reference category is named: row (after its label) | note (the general note) | none. Takes one of row | note | none. In apa: row.

reference.label

the word before the reference category: reference | ref. Takes any text. In apa: reference.

variable.headings

how a dummy-coded variable's label row is set: plain | italic | bold. Takes one of plain | italic | bold. In apa: plain; in report: bold.

group.headings

how a heading row is set: italic | bold | plain. Takes one of italic | bold | plain. In apa: italic.

[logistic]: a logistic regression table

title

the title when the call gives none; {outcome} is the outcome's label. Takes any text. In apa: Logistic Regression Coefficients Predicting {outcome}.

columns

the columns of each model, in order: b, se, or (the odds ratio), p, wald, ci (for the odds ratio), beta.gelman. Takes one or more of b, se, or, p, wald, ci, beta.gelman, in order, separated by commas. In apa: b, se, or, p.

columns.last

columns added to the last model only, or none. Takes one or more of b, se, or, p, wald, ci, beta.gelman, in order, separated by commas; or none. In apa: none.

stub.label

the first column's head. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: Predictor.

b.label

the head of the b column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: b.

se.label

the head of the se column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: SE.

or.label

the head of the or column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: OR.

p.label

the head of the p column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: p.

wald.label

the head of the wald column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: Wald.

ci.label

the head of the ci column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: 95% CI for OR.

beta.gelman.label

the head of the beta.gelman column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: \(\beta\)*.

ci.style

one: the interval in one column, [LL, UL] | two: LL and UL. Takes one of one | two. In apa: one.

intercept

the constant's row, first in the table: yes | no. Takes one of yes | no. In apa: yes.

intercept.label

the constant's row label. Takes any text. In apa: Constant.

fit.rows

the fit rows under the predictors, in order: chisq (the model chi-square), nagelkerke, cox.snell, neg2ll, aic, n, or none. Takes one or more of chisq, nagelkerke, cox.snell, neg2ll, aic, n, in order, separated by commas; or none. In apa: chisq, nagelkerke.

reference

where a dummy-coded variable's reference category is named: row (after its label) | note (the general note) | none. Takes one of row | note | none. In apa: row.

reference.label

the word before the reference category: reference | ref. Takes any text. In apa: reference.

variable.headings

how a dummy-coded variable's label row is set: plain | italic | bold. Takes one of plain | italic | bold. In apa: plain; in report: bold.

group.headings

how a heading row is set: italic | bold | plain. Takes one of italic | bold | plain. In apa: italic.

[correlation]: a correlation table

title

the title when the call gives none. Takes any text. In apa: Descriptive Statistics and Correlations for Study Variables.

columns

the columns before the correlations, in order: n, mean, sd, or none. Takes one or more of n, mean, sd, in order, separated by commas; or none. In apa: n, mean, sd.

stub.label

the first column's head. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: Variable.

n.label

the head of the n column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: n.

mean.label

the head of the mean column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: M.

sd.label

the head of the sd column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: SD.

lower.triangle

yes: each correlation once, below the diagonal | no: both triangles. Takes one of yes | no. In apa: yes.

r.stars

yes: asterisks on each correlation for its p-value, explained under the table | no. Takes one of yes | no. In apa: yes.

method.note

yes: the note names a Spearman or Kendall table's correlations | no. Takes one of yes | no. In apa: yes.

[ttest]: a t-test table

title

the title when the call gives none; {group} is the grouping variable's label. Takes any text. In apa: Means, Standard Deviations, and *t* Tests by {group}.

columns

the columns, in order: each group's n, mean and sd, then t (with its df), p, d (Cohen's d), diff (the mean difference) and ci (its confidence interval). Takes one or more of n, mean, sd, t, p, d, diff, ci, in order, separated by commas. In apa: mean, sd, t, p, d.

stub.label

the first column's head. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: Variable.

n.label

the head of the n column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: n.

mean.label

the head of the mean column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: M.

sd.label

the head of the sd column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: SD.

t.label

the head of the t column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: t.

df.label

the head of the df column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: df.

df.position

head: the df in the statistic's head, t(101), when every row shares them, else a df column | column: a df column. Takes one of head | column. In apa: head; in report: column.

p.label

the head of the p column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: p.

d.label

the head of the d column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: d.

diff.label

the head of the diff column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: Mean difference.

ci.label

the head of the ci column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: 95% CI.

ci.style

one: the interval in one column, [LL, UL] | two: LL and UL. Takes one of one | two. In apa: one.

group.spanner

yes: the grouping variable's label over the groups' columns | no. Takes one of yes | no. In apa: yes.

test.note

yes: the note says when a test is Welch's or a paired test | no. Takes one of yes | no. In apa: yes.

[anova]: an ANOVA table

title

the title when the call gives none; {group} is the grouping variable's label. Takes any text. In apa: Means, Standard Deviations, and One-Way Analyses of Variance by {group}.

columns

the columns, in order: each group's n, mean and sd, then f (with its df), p, eta2. Takes one or more of n, mean, sd, f, p, eta2, in order, separated by commas. In apa: mean, sd, f, p, eta2.

stub.label

the first column's head. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: Variable.

n.label

the head of the n column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: n.

mean.label

the head of the mean column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: M.

sd.label

the head of the sd column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: SD.

f.label

the head of the f column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: F.

df.label

the head of the df column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: df.

df.position

head: the df in the statistic's head, F(3, 99), when every row shares them, else a df column | column: a df column. Takes one of head | column. In apa: head; in report: column.

p.label

the head of the p column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: p.

eta2.label

the head of the eta2 column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: \(\eta^2\).

group.spanner

yes: the grouping variable's label over the groups' columns | no. Takes one of yes | no. In apa: yes.

test.note

yes: the note says when a test is Welch's | no. Takes one of yes | no. In apa: yes.

[crosstab]: a crosstab

title

the title when the call gives none; {group} is the column variable's label. Takes any text. In apa: Frequencies and Percentages by {group}.

columns

each group's columns, in order: n, percent. Takes one or more of n, percent, in order, separated by commas. In apa: n, percent.

total

yes: a Total column after the groups | no. Takes one of yes | no. In apa: yes.

percent.base

what a percentage is of: column (each group's cases) | row (each category's) | total (all cases). Takes one of column | row | total. In apa: column.

test.columns

the chi-square test's columns on each variable's row, in order: chisq, df, p, v (Cramer's V), or none. Takes one or more of chisq, df, p, v, in order, separated by commas; or none. In apa: chisq, df, p, v.

stub.label

the first column's head. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: Variable.

n.label

the head of the n column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: n.

percent.label

the head of the percent column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: %.

total.label

the head over the Total column. Takes any text. In apa: Total.

chisq.label

the head of the chisq column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: \(\chi^2\).

df.label

the head of the df column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: df.

p.label

the head of the p column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: p.

v.label

the head of the v column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: V.

group.spanner

yes: the column variable's label over the groups' columns | no. Takes one of yes | no. In apa: yes.

variable.headings

how each variable's label row is set: plain | italic | bold. Takes one of plain | italic | bold. In apa: plain; in report: bold.

title

columns

the columns, in order: mean, sd, item.total (the corrected item-total correlation), alpha.if.deleted. Takes one or more of mean, sd, item.total, alpha.if.deleted, in order, separated by commas. In apa: mean, sd, item.total, alpha.if.deleted.

stub.label

mean.label

sd.label

item.total.label

the head of the item.total column; *r* sets r in italics. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: Item-total *r*.

alpha.if.deleted.label

the head of the alpha.if.deleted column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: \(\alpha\) if item deleted.

alpha

yes: Cronbach's alpha in the note, or after each scale's name when the table holds several | no. Takes one of yes | no. In apa: yes.

item.total.note

yes: the note says what the item.total column is | no. Takes one of yes | no. In apa: yes.

group.headings

how a scale's name row is set: italic | bold | plain. Takes one of italic | bold | plain. In apa: italic.

[multiresponse]: a multiple-response table

title

the title when the call gives none; {set} is the text the items' labels share, else Multiple-Response Set. Takes any text. In apa: {set}.

columns

the columns, in order: n (the cases in the category), percent (of N). Takes one or more of n, percent, in order, separated by commas. In apa: n, percent.

stub.label

the first column's head. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: Category.

n.label

the head of the n column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: n.

percent.label

the head of the percent column. Takes any text, or nothing. In apa: %.

none.label

the label of the row of cases in none of the categories. Takes any text. In apa: None of these.

choice.note

yes: the note says a case can be counted in more than one category, so the percentages sum to more than 100 | no. Takes one of yes | no. In apa: yes.

[plot]: a chart

font

the typeface of a chart's text. Takes any text. In apa: Arial.

size

the size of a chart's text, in points. Takes a number from 6 to 72. In apa: 10.

palette

the colors of a chart's bars, lines and points, in order: greys (595959 for one series, 404040 and A6A6A6 for two, more in steps from 404040) or the colors to use. Takes greys, or one or more colors in order, separated by commas, each a color name such as navy or six hex digits such as 1F3864. In apa: greys.

gridlines

light lines across a chart at the axes' labels: none | horizontal | vertical | both. Takes one of none | horizontal | vertical | both. In apa: none; in report: horizontal.

grid.color

the color of the gridlines. Takes a color name such as lightblue, or six hex digits such as ADD8E6. In apa: D9D9D9.

axis.lines

the axis lines drawn: both | x (the bottom axis) | y (the left axis) | none. Takes one of both | x | y | none. In apa: both; in report: x.

legend.position

where a chart's legend goes, with its title: right | top | bottom (top and bottom start at the left) | none. Takes one of right | top | bottom | none. In apa: right; in report: top.

values

yes: each bar's value just beyond its end, on a chart of one series, such as a bar chart of one variable | no. Takes one of yes | no. In apa: yes.

values.grouped

the same on a chart of several series, such as grouped bars: no | yes. Takes one of no | yes. In apa: no.

values.stacked

yes: a 100% stacked bar's percentages inside its segments, none in a segment under 6 percent | no. Takes one of no | yes. In apa: no.

values.decimals

the decimal places of a percentage a chart shows, on a pie's slices, at a ranked bar's end or in a stacked bar's segments: 0 or 1. Takes a whole number from 0 to 1. In apa: 0.

pie.max

the most categories a pie or a donut chart shows; a variable with more stops, with the line that draws a bar chart. Takes a whole number from 2 to 6. In apa: 6.

width

a figure's width in a Word file, in inches. Takes a number from 1 to 20. In apa: 6.

height

a figure's height in a Word file, in inches. Takes a number from 1 to 20. In apa: 4.

resolution

the resolution of a figure's picture, in dots per inch. Takes a whole number from 72 to 1200. In apa: 300.

data.file

yes: the numbers each chart shows are written to an Excel file beside the Word file, a sheet per figure | no. Takes one of no | yes. In apa: no.

vector.file

a vector file of each figure beside the Word file, as a publisher may ask for one: none | pdf | eps. Takes one of none | pdf | eps. In apa: none.
